LONGUEUIL, Quebec, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Polara, a North American provider of charging infrastructure, software and energy services for electric fleets, today announced that it ranked number 139 on the Deloitte Technology Fast 500™, a ranking of the 500 fastest-growing tech companies in North America, now in its 32nd year. Polara grew 515% during 2022 to 2025.

“Our growth comes from solving the full operational challenge, not just installing chargers”, said Polara’s Chief Executive Officer, Sébastien Fournier. “We bring together infrastructure, fleet operations, software and energy expertise to help customers deploy and operate electric fleet. Our smart platform Cleo optimizes charging sessions and strengthens the economics of electrification.”

Polara’s growth is rooted in the expertise gained through complex fleet-electrification projects across the United States and Canada. This hands-on experience allows the company to design solutions around each fleet’s operational, charging and energy requirements rather than treating charging as a stand-alone equipment purchase.

A key technology supporting this approach is Cleo, Polara’s smart charging and energy-management platform. Cleo connects vehicles, charging stations, buildings and power-grid signals, helping fleets schedule charging around vehicle availability and site constraints while managing demand and energy costs.

On the hardware side, CHRGPK, Polara’s proprietary modular power platform for fleet depots, delivers more than 95% efficiency, IEEE-compliant harmonic mitigation and utility-grade metering and protection, making depots easier to connect, maintain and expand as fleets grow.

Scale demonstrated in the field

Polara’s North American footprint now includes:

  • 165 charging-infrastructure projects delivered;
  • 290 sites managed through Cleo, optimizing thousands of charging stations;
  • Nearly 150 electric fleets have entrusted Polara with the management of their carbon credits.

This scale is reflected in projects that address different fleet, energy and grid requirements:

  • New York State’s largest electric school bus fast-charging project for GVC Ltd.;
  • Vehicle-to-grid (V2G) infrastructure for Fremont Unified School District in California;
  • Canada’s first municipal vehicle-to-everything (V2X) charging station in Victoriaville, Quebec.

Extending the business case through energy and carbon markets

Beyond infrastructure and smart charging, Polara helps fleets across North America unlock additional value from their transition to electric vehicles and equipment. Through carbon credit management, Polara enables fleets generate recurring revenue that complements energy and maintenance savings, strengthening the business case for fleet electrification.

“The next stage of fleet electrification will be measured by operational and financial performance,” said David Cantin, Vice President, Finance at Polara. “By optimizing charging, accessing energy services and capturing carbon-market value, we help customers turn electrification into a long-term operating advantage.”

“The 2026 rankings demonstrate that established momentum and breakthrough growth can drive sustained market leadership,” said Justin Yahr, Audit & Assurance partner and National Emerging Growth Company leader, Deloitte & Touche LLP. “Nearly 70% of this year’s award winners returned as repeat honorees, reflecting the power of disciplined and sustained execution. More than 30% made the list for the first time, illustrating how quickly new players are shaping their respective sectors. Furthermore, private companies represented almost 80% of the list, a clear indication that the agility and strategic focus of private enterprises remain essential to scaling in competitive markets.”

Polara provides charging infrastructure, software and energy services for electric vehicle fleets in the United States and Canada. Its integrated offering spans fleet and site analysis, charging infrastructure with its CHRGPK power platform, smart charging and energy management through Cleo, V2G and V2X applications, and carbon-credit monetization through Polara Carbon. Polara works with fleet operators, school transportation providers, manufacturers, municipalities and public-sector organizations to improve charging reliability, control energy costs and unlock additional value from electric assets.
